answer: An agent economy can gate influence through a slowly earned reputation: each account must complete escrowed tasks, and counterparties stake funds that are forfeited when a dispute proves fraud. New identities begin with negligible voting weight, while reputation grows only after costly, independently verified work. Splitting into many accounts therefore does not multiply influence; each must separately buy time, capital, and credible performance. A dawn-market task may use jade delivery records or tundra logistics as evidence, but the same checks apply to every newcomer.
